picks.title: The $15 billion ad-powered AI startup your doctor may already be using
picks.take: OpenEvidence is valued at $15 billion, is reportedly already in your doctor's pocket, and is funded by ads, with questions about accuracy attached. Nothing says evidence-based medicine like a sponsor wondering what the clinician is about to prescribe.

picks.title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study
picks.take: A study asks whether ambient AI scribes reduce documentation burden and also improve financial productivity in primary care. Finally, the note-writing robot gets a productivity target, so the doctor can enjoy the time saved by seeing more patients.

picks.title: AI doctors' orders come with a sky-high bill
picks.take: Nature reports that AI doctors' orders come with a sky-high bill. The technology that promised to cut costs has discovered the one thing healthcare reliably scales: the invoice.

picks.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment
picks.take: A randomised crossover experiment examines how clinicians rely on AI advice in imaging. Medicine's long-awaited second opinion arrives, and we now study whether anyone is still forming a first one.

picks.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
picks.take: Nature Medicine looks at putting conversational AI to the test in primary care. Testing before deployment is a bold and refreshing sequence of events, and we should encourage it before someone stops it.

picks.title: AI drug firm Pathos raises $237 million, pushing valuation to $3 billion
picks.take: Pathos raises $237 million at a $3 billion valuation, combining Tempus data, Pathos AI and BMS drug development. Three organizations, one pipeline, and a valuation that arrives well ahead of the clinical trial results.

picks.title: Avoiding a 2-Tier AI Ecosystem in Health Care
picks.take: JAMA Health Forum warns about avoiding a two-tier AI ecosystem in health care. Medicine has been so successful at equitable access that it naturally worries about whether the algorithms will be the exception.

picks.title: What’s the deal with Isomorphic Labs?
picks.take: STAT asks what the deal is with Isomorphic Labs, and what its high valuation says about AI in drug development and the cost of care. The valuation is certain; the molecules are still being worked out.

picks.title: Keeping artificial intelligence agents within the clinical task
picks.take: The Lancet Digital Health argues that AI agents should be kept within the clinical task. A reasonable request, given that every other staff member also needs a job description and a badge.

picks.title: Association of ambient artificial intelligence scribe availability with patient instruction documentation and readability in ambulatory care
picks.take: A study asks whether ambient AI scribe availability changes patient instruction documentation and readability in ambulatory care. Patients may finally get instructions they can read, written by software that the physician then has to proofread after clinic.
